text:
Sam: Quick thread — trying to pick regions for Q3 reserved commits. Short version: SFO (A100-heavy), ORD, DUB, SIN options. Looking at net egress, interconnect fees, and spot eviction risk. Anyone seen a clear cost/latency winner?

Olga: If you care about unit $/token ORD with reserved commitments is lowest — but egress to EU customers from ORD adds ~12% when we include cross-region outbound. DUB wins for EU latency and avoids interconnect fees for EU traffic. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Mike: FYI our current GPU mixes differ — SFO uses A100s for high throughput, ORD uses a mix of A10G-ish instances. Packing density in SFO is better (higher util) but reserved SKU premiums are ~18% vs ORD.

infra-bot: billing-scan report ready
```
region  reserved_hours  on_demand_hours  avg_unit_cost_usd
SFO     43200           12000            0.021
ORD     50400            8000            0.018
DUB     46800           14000            0.019
SIN     36000           18000            0.023
``` 

Henry: Two operational notes — SIN has higher spot churn last month (preemptions up 2.3x) and network packet drops on a subset of racks (ticket #7834). If we put steady-state inference there, we need >20% buffer.

Karen: Also watch cross-region internal NAT egress in DUB->US flows. If we run EU origin for EU + failover to US, egress costs can spike; recommend sticky routing to avoid unnecessary cross-region failovers.

Olga: TL;DR: ORD lowest $/unit but DUB best for EU latency / simpler egress footprint. SFO better for high-util US west customers. SIN only if APAC demand justifies buffer + premium. 

Sam: Proposed plan: commit ORD baseline for US core, reserve DUB for EU steady state, keep a small burst pool in SFO, avoid SIN commits until eviction shows stable. Can finance do a 12-month ORD+DUB blended commit? @Olga

Olga: Yes we can model a blended 12mo commit. I'll run a sensitivity with +/-20% traffic and include interconnect line items. Will post numbers by EOD. :mag:

Sam: Great — will draft placement policy and a simple routing override to keep EU -> DUB sticky. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
